title: Nominal Effective Exchange Rate (NEER, BIS broad)
description: Trade-weighted nominal value of the Indian rupee against 64 trading partners' currencies, BIS broad effective exchange rate index, 2020 = 100. A rise is rupee appreciation. Daily from 1996 and monthly from 1994. It summarises the external price pressure on exports, imports and inflation far better than USD/INR alone, and is a timely nowcasting input for trade competitiveness and imported inflation.
source: Bank for International Settlements (effective exchange rate indices)

qna.question: What are the NEER and REER?
qna.answer: The nominal effective exchange rate (NEER) is a trade-weighted average of the rupee's bilateral exchange rates against a basket of partner currencies. The real effective exchange rate (REER) adjusts the NEER for relative consumer-price inflation between India and its partners.^An increase means the rupee has appreciated against the basket (a loss of price competitiveness); a decrease means depreciation.

qna.question: How should I read them?
qna.answer: The REER is the usual competitiveness gauge: values well above 100 indicate an overvalued rupee relative to the base year, and sustained depreciation of the REER tends to support exports and import substitution, while appreciation lowers imported inflation. The NEER is available daily and reacts quickly to the dollar and other major currencies, so it is useful for tracking real-time external conditions.^These indices complement USD/INR, which looks at a single bilateral rate.

qna.question: Definitions and caveats
qna.answer: These are the Bank for International Settlements (BIS) effective exchange rate indices for India: broad basket of 64 economies, base 2020 = 100. They are NOT the RBI's 6-currency or 40-currency indices (base 2015-16 = 100), so levels differ from RBI's published figures although direction is usually similar.^BIS revises the latest months as price and trade-weight data arrive; the daily NEER is nominal only, because consumer-price deflators are available monthly. Daily dates are the BIS reference date; monthly values are stamped on the first of the month.
